content:
maria: Heads up — enterprise onboarding asked for an enterprise/dedicated canary flow that guarantees tenant isolation. They want per-tenant traffic splits, but also a hard safety guard if a tenant spikes error rate. Can we sketch the UX + runtime checks?

devin: Can we clarify requirements? do they want strict network isolation or just traffic % and auto rollback?

maria: Mostly per-tenant traffic % with automatic rollback when SLOs break. Also they want the option to pin a tenant to a fallback model pool (no shared burst) if misbehaving.

ashok: Runtime constraints: for Dedicated we already have per-tenant queues, but the canary path currently shares model instances in the pool. We can add traffic-slicing on the router to send X% of a tenant's requests to the new variant.

kevin: Important: define metrics and thresholds. propose: error_rate > 1% OR p95 increase > 30% relative to baseline for 5 minutes triggers rollback. Also protect overall instance CPU/GPU saturation (>= 80%) to avoid collateral.

jess: For console UX, product prefers a simple slider: Start at 0% -> 1% -> auto-ramp to target with pause on anomalies. Need a manual override and 'pin to fallback' checkbox.

devin: Agreed on slider. Backend needs to expose these knobs: target_percent, step_percent, step_interval, metric_rules (type, threshold, window), fallback_policy. Example config draft:```json
{
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "variant": "v2",
  "target_percent": 20,
  "step_percent": 1,
  "step_interval_sec": 300,
  "metrics": [
    {"name": "error_rate", "op": ">", "value": 0.01, "window_sec": 300},
    {"name": "latency_p95_rel", "op": ">", "value": 0.3, "window_sec": 300}
  ],
  "fallback": {"type": "fallback_pool", "pin": true}
}
```

maria: That looks good. A couple notes: latency_p95_rel needs a baseline per-tenant (recent 24h) or a control group. We shouldn't compare to global baseline.

ashok: We can store per-tenant baseline in timeseries DB and compute relative deltas on rollouts. But computing that for every step might be expensive — suggest we only compute baselines at rollout start and update every hour.

kevin: Also add a throttle guard: max_requests_per_sec cap for the canary variant so a sudden spike from sampling doesn't overload infra. If cap exceeded, pause ramp and alert.

jess: UX question: show real-time telemetry for canary vs baseline in the console — error rate, p95, token consumption. Need to wire tenant tag into all metrics and traces.

devin: We'll need a router change to tag sampled requests with rollout_id and tenant_id so metrics pipeline can aggregate. Also ensure sampling is deterministic per-request-id when using sticky sampling (so same user sees consistent model).

maria: Operationally, we should provide two fail modes: automatic rollback (on rule breach) and degrade-to-fallback (send all to fallback_pool but keep variant warm). Customer can choose. Default should be rollback to be safest.

ashok: Implementation plan: 1) router: per-tenant traffic splitter + throttle 2) control plane: rollout API + config store 3) metrics: rollout_id tagging + baseline lookup 4) console: slider + live chart + manual controls.

kevin: SRE asks: add kill-switch with org-level throttle that prevents any tenant rollout from exceeding reserved capacity. Also, render warnings if tenant's dedicated quota is near limit.

jess: From biz: customers may want canary across dedicated and shared pools simultaneously. Need clear labels in UI and a dropdown for target deployment type.

devin: One tricky part — quota accounting. Traffic to canary still consumes tokens and GPU. For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, we must bill against their quota. We'll add a 'canary_billing_tag' to requests.

maria: Great. Who wants to own API schema and initial console mock? I can do the mock. @devin will you draft the rollout API?

devin: I'll draft API. Plan to add endpoints: POST /rollouts, GET /rollouts/{id}/status, POST /rollouts/{id}/pause, POST /rollouts/{id}/rollback. I'll share a WIP spec later today.

ashok: I'll prototype router changes and a toggle to enable per-tenant sampling.

kevin: I'll write SLO-based alerting templates and the automated rollback hook.

deploy-bot: Deploy checklist created: rollout-api v1 -> staging, router feature flag -> off by default, telemetry tagging -> feature branch.

maria: SGTM. Next sync in #eng-platform tomorrow 10am to review API + console mock. If anyone has compliance/regression concerns, flag them now. :slightly_smiling_face:
